findings.message: `desired()` now writes `meta.ownerEmail`, which is the raw git author or Owner-line email, into `delivery.proposal.meta` for every spec proposal. That includes emails of committers who are not people in amax. The delivery.proposal retention entry (module.ts:69) puts `meta` under `keep` as sync state with no person in it. So these emails are never anonymised and erasure cannot find them by subject. They also reach the append-only `core.trace_event` through the raw sync_specclaw args. Fix: do not persist the email. Resolve it to an owner id at push time and store only that id, or a keyed hash if staleness needs the input. Strip `owner`/`author` from what gets traced, or list the key under the retention entry's fields.
findings.scenario: An outside contributor stranger@example.test adds change.md → the CI push stores meta.ownerEmail='stranger@example.test' on FLT-515. A later erasure request or the 7-year anonymise leaves that email in meta and in the trace forever.

findings.message: AC-7 says the owner is the Owner line, else the change's author. Only the plugin and CI fill `author`. The self-sync (`sync/bin.ts` → `readSpecclaw` file reader → `syncSpecclaw`) never sets it, but it uses the same 'follow the repo' upsert. So for a change with no Owner line, the self-sync resolves nobody and clears the owner the push set. The two writers disagree about the same proposal. Fix: fill `author` in bin.ts with the same git lookup (share `authorsOf`), or have the self-sync leave the owner alone when it has no author information.
findings.scenario: Change 512-x has no Owner line and was added by nimal@lumenlabs.test. The CI push sets the owner to Nimal Silva. `pnpm --filter @amax/delivery sync:specclaw` then sees ownerEmail=null, repoOwnerStale is true, and it rewrites the owner to Unassigned. The next CI push sets Nimal again.

findings.message: `authorsOf` swallows any `git log` failure and returns `author: null`. That is the same value as 'the repo names nobody'. The server follows the repo until a person sets the owner, so a failed lookup clears an existing owner. A shallow history has the same effect, or worse: the graft commit shows every file as Added, so its author becomes the owner of everything. Fix: tell 'could not read' apart from 'no author' (for example, leave `author` undefined or flag the record), and have the server keep the stored owner when the author is unknown. Fail or warn when the history is shallow.
findings.scenario: git log errors for 513-identity (a missing rev, or a grafted clone) → author=null → repoOwnerStale(cur owner=Nimal, repo=null) is true → the push rewrites FLT-513 to Unassigned and says nothing.

findings.message: `upsertSpecProposal` now rewrites `owner_user_id`/`owner_name` on every sync that the person-set flag doesn't stop, including clearing them. But the `before`/`after` it returns (and that push.ts and syncProposal audit) hold only phase, tasksDone, title and sha. An owner change or removal by a sync leaves no audit record of who was owner before or after, and it raises no event, so nobody hears of it. Fix: add `owner` (the name, plus the id or null) to `before` and `after`.
findings.scenario: FLT-521 is owned by Nimal Silva through its repo author. The repo's author email is changed to stranger@example.test and pushed → the owner is cleared. The delivery.proposal.sync audit row reads before {phase, tasksDone, title}, after {phase, tasksDone, title, sha}, and nothing shows Nimal was removed.

findings.message: 'A person set the owner' has three paths, but the test drives only `updateProposal`. Untested: `setOwnerIn` (accepting a Suggested owner, and its undo, which can set the owner to null) and the 0021 backfill that flags owners set before the column existed. If any of them failed to set `owner_set_by_person`, the next sync would silently overwrite the person's decision. Fix: make the 'then it stands' test table-driven over update_proposal, Suggested-owner accept, Suggested-owner undo to null, and a row backfilled from a pre-0021 delivery.proposal.update audit row. Drive each through the real path.
findings.scenario: Delete `owner_set_by_person = true` from setOwnerIn → every test stays green. In production, accepting 'Suggested owner: Maya' is undone by the next CI push.

findings.message: The rule for which email names the owner (`r.owner ?? r.author ?? null`) is written twice: in `desired()` at line 28 and again in the staleness pre-pass. Make it one helper so the staleness check and the write can't drift apart.

A branch counts as merged only when `merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> HEAD` is true. That holds for merge and fast-forward merges only. GitHub squash and rebase merges leave the branch's commits out of main's ancestry. Such a branch is left out only once main has archived its change. A squash-merged branch whose change is still open on main keeps getting pushed. The AC-1 test covers only `--ff-only`. Fix: also treat a branch as merged when its change folder on main matches the branch's tree (for example, `git diff --quiet origin/<b> HEAD -- .specclaw/changes/<dir>`), or when main's commit is newer than the branch's for that folder. Test squash and rebase merges as well as ff.
findings.scenario: specclaw/120-x is squash-merged into main and the remote branch is kept. Main has 120-x at 'building' from a newer commit. Every CI run still pushes specclaw/120-x. The push is skipped as stale with needsReview, so the Repo sync card shows 'Needs you' after every merge. That is the noise AC-1 was meant to remove.
